data.name: Liechtenstein
data.summary: Liechtenstein taxes wealth instead of investment income. Net wealth (excluding foreign real estate) is converted into a deemed income of 4% (Sollertrag) and taxed with other income at the progressive state rate (top 8%) plus a municipal surcharge of 150%-250% of the state tax; at the minimum surcharge of 150% this is a wealth tax of up to 0.8% a year (0.896% at 180%). In return, dividends, interest and gains on shares and other movable private assets are exempt from income tax. There is no inheritance or gift tax. Liechtenstein real estate gains bear a separate tax of up to 24%. The main obstacle is residence: permits are scarce for EEA nationals and very limited for others.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (wealth and income tax)
regimes.description: Combined wealth and income tax (Vermögens- und Erwerbssteuer) under the Tax Act (SteG, LGBl. 2010.340). Wealth is taxed through a 4% deemed return added to taxable income; actual returns on that wealth are exempt.
regimes.eligibility: Domicile (intention to stay permanently) or habitual residence of more than six months in Liechtenstein. Requires a residence permit, which is the main practical barrier.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on movable and immovable private assets are exempt from income tax (Art. 15(2)(m) SteG), as are gains on shares (Art. 15(2)(o)) and gains on foreign real estate (Art. 15(2)(l)). Gains on Liechtenstein real estate are taxed separately by the real estate gains tax: the income tax tariff for single persons (top 8%) plus a fixed 200% surcharge, up to 24%. Capital losses are not deductible.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: All private capital gains on movable assets exempt. Real estate gains tax: the basic allowance of the single-person tariff (CHF 15,855) applies.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Assets held as private assets. Business assets follow different rules (anti-abuse rules for passive low-taxed foreign participations).
capital_gains.regional_differences: Municipal surcharge differs by municipality but does not affect exempt gains; the real estate gains surcharge is a fixed 200%.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Business-asset participations in passive, low-taxed foreign entities can lose the exemption. Indirect transfers of real estate companies trigger real estate gains tax.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Movable assets, shares and foreign real estate: exempt under Art. 15(2)(l), (m), (o) SteG. Liechtenstein real estate: Art. 42 applies the Art. 19(1)(a) tariff (top marginal 8% from CHF 211,401) and Art. 43 adds a 200% surcharge instead of the municipal surcharge: 8% x 3 = 24%. Headline = that 24%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Professional securities dealing would be business income (taxed via the income tax), but the private-asset exemption is broad; no recharacterisation guidance was found.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign securities: same exemption. Foreign real estate: excluded from wealth tax (Art. 10(e)) and its gains exempt (Art. 15(2)(l)), with progression reservation for the rate (Art. 21).

dividends.summary: Dividends and profit shares from participations in legal entities are exempt from income tax for private shareholders (Art. 15(2)(n) SteG), as are all returns on wealth subject to wealth tax (Art. 15(1)(a)). The wealth tax (deemed return) replaces dividend tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign withholding tax on dividends cannot be credited because no Liechtenstein tax arises on them; treaty reduction at source is the only relief.
open_questions: Size of Liechtenstein's treaty network and whether foreign withholding can be reduced for residents was not verified (Liechtenstein has a limited network, including Switzerland, Austria, Germany, the UK and Luxembourg, from general knowledge).
dividends.rate_basis: Art. 15(2)(n) SteG exempts profit shares; Art. 15(1)(a) exempts returns on wealth subject to wealth tax. Rate 0.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Liechtenstein abolished its dividend coupon tax in 2011 (from general knowledge; PwC's withholding section not opened); companies distribute without withholding.
dividends.treaty_network: Small treaty network; not verified in this session.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 12.5% profit tax with a CHF 1,800 minimum tax. Private asset structures (PVS) pay only the minimum tax but have no treaty access. No structure is modelled: a resident already pays no tax on dividends and gains; a controlled foundation or company is attributed to the founder for wealth tax, and moving assets into an opaque foundation that leaves the wealth tax base costs a one-off dedication tax of 3.5% plus municipal surcharge (8.75%-9.8%, up to 10.5%), after which distributions are taxable income for resident beneficiaries, so the saving of about 0.8% a year takes a decade or more to recover and is not a commonly used robust structure for residents.

wealth_tax.summary: Wealth tax is levied through the income tax: worldwide net wealth (excluding foreign real estate and foreign permanent establishments) is multiplied by a 4% standard return (Sollertrag, Art. 5 SteG) and taxed together with other income at the progressive state tariff (marginal 1%-8%), plus a municipal surcharge set each year by the municipality between 150% and 250% of the state tax (PwC: currently 150%-180%). For a married couple whose only income is the deemed return, the effective marginal wealth tax rises to 0.8% at a 150% surcharge (0.896% at 180%).
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Household goods and private cars up to CHF 52,800 for a married couple; foreign real estate exempt. The income tax basic allowance (CHF 31,710 joint) makes the first ~CHF 792,750 of wealth tax-free if there is no other income.
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: All residents taxed in the ordinary way.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: The municipal surcharge varies (legal range 150%-250%); the brackets assume 150%.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Because the deemed return is added to other income, earned or pension income pushes the deemed return into higher bands sooner. Transfers into a structure that leaves the wealth tax base (e.g. an opaque foundation without proxy taxation) bear a one-off 3.5% dedication tax (Art. 13) plus the municipal surcharge. Lump-sum taxation on expenditure (Art. 30-34) replaces wealth and income tax for qualifying newcomers (see open questions).

open_questions: The 2026 municipal surcharge for Vaduz was not verified (llv.li blocked); brackets assume the statutory minimum 150%. Scale rates by (1+surcharge)/2.5 for other municipalities.
Brackets assume no income besides the deemed return and joint assessment of a married couple (Art. 19(1)(c) tariff).

components.name: Wealth tax via 4% deemed return (Vermögenssteuer als Sollertrag)
components.notes: Derived from Art. 19(1)(c) SteG (married couples): marginal state rates 0/1/3/4/5/6/6.5/7/8% with income thresholds CHF 31,710 / 42,280 / 84,560 / 147,980 / 211,400 / 274,820 / 338,240 / 422,800. Wealth thresholds = income thresholds / 0.04. Effective wealth rate = 4% x state rate x 2.5 (150% municipal surcharge). Base excludes foreign real estate (Art. 10(e)).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No separate property tax; Liechtenstein real estate is part of the wealth tax base.

inheritance.summary: Liechtenstein levies no inheritance, estate or gift tax. Inheritances and gifts are also exempt from income tax (Art. 15(2)(c) SteG). The heirs simply include the assets in their own wealth tax base afterwards.
inheritance.important_exceptions: A 3.5% dedication tax (Widmungssteuer, Art. 13 SteG) plus municipal surcharge (up to 10.5% in total per PwC) applies when assets are transferred to an entity or structure so that they leave the wealth tax base and the beneficial interests cannot be valued; not relevant to direct gifts to children.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; gifts are exempt from income tax. Only the dedication tax applies to transfers into structures outside the wealth tax base.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on any assets; foreign estate taxes of situs countries may apply.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident with a domicile in Liechtenstein (living there with the intention to stay) or a habitual residence of more than six months.

routes.name: EEA nationals: residence permit within annual quota
routes.requirements: Liechtenstein is in the EEA but restricts free movement of persons: residence permits for EEA nationals who do not work in Liechtenstein are subject to an annual quota, part of which is allocated by lottery. Details not verified in this session (official llv.li pages were blocked).

routes.name: Third-country nationals
routes.requirements: Very limited: permits are granted only exceptionally (e.g. senior managers or persons with a significant economic interest in Liechtenstein). No investor or golden-visa programme known. Not verified in this session.

corporate.summary: Flat 12.5% profit tax on worldwide income; CHF 1,800 annual minimum tax (creditable), waived for small operating companies. Dividends and capital gains on participations generally exempt. Pillar Two 15% top-up for large groups. Private asset structures (PVS) pay only the minimum tax.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the ten priced houses of 5.5 rooms or more (Swiss room count; about 4+ bedrooms) offered to let across Liechtenstein on 15 Oct 2026 on the two Liechtenstein portals, immoboerse.li (ITW, all 13 house rentals in the country) and nemo.li (14 house rentals), duplicates removed: Schaan 6.5 rooms 3,450; Mauren 6.5 rooms 3,350; Balzers 7.5-room terraced houses from 2,750; Gamprin-Bendern 5.5 rooms 2,690; Schellenberg 5.5 rooms 2,500; Nendeln 5.5 rooms 2,500; Schaan 7.5 rooms (older house) 2,500; Eschen 6.5 rooms 2,400; Ruggell 6.5 rooms 2,400; Balzers 6.5 rooms 1,900 (CHF a month, mostly net of utilities). Not prime: none of the priced houses is in Vaduz. Engel & Völkers' three Vaduz houses the same day were a 5.5-room detached house (price on request), a premium 5.5-room house in the villa quarter (let, price on request) and a 5.5-room Städtle house (let, CHF 2,950 total rent); a 7.5-room, 225 m² Schaan house was price on request. A prime Vaduz family house therefore likely rents above this median. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

data.us_citizen_notes: No US-Liechtenstein income tax treaty (a TIEA and FATCA IGA exist). Liechtenstein's wealth-based tax is not an income tax on specific items, so US foreign tax credits for it are doubtful; US citizens pay full US tax on gains and dividends.
open_questions: Lump-sum taxation on expenditure (Art. 30-34 SteG: 25% of total annual expenditure, replacing wealth and income tax; for non-citizens arriving for the first time or after 10 years away who do not work in Liechtenstein; Liechtenstein real estate stays subject to wealth tax) was not modelled as a special regime because no typical or minimum expenditure base could be verified; the implementing ordinance was not read.
Residence permit rules (EEA quota/lottery, third-country access) need confirmation from the Migration and Passport Office.
Vaduz municipal surcharge for 2026 not verified.

Prime rent is the CHF 2,500 median of ten ordinary 5.5+-room houses across Liechtenstein (immoboerse.li, nemo.li, 15 Oct 2026); no priced Vaduz house was listed (Engel & Völkers' Vaduz houses were price on request or let). A Vaduz/Schaan prime figure from an agency would make the rent more representative.

succession.name: Liechtenstein
succession.summary: Children and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share, and a will cannot remove it, though a foundation or trust is a common planning route. Liechtenstein has its own trust and foundation law, and the Hague Trusts Convention is in force. A reform to the Pflichtteil is before parliament.
succession.reserved_share: Pflichtteil under the ABGB (about art. 762 ff.): descendants and spouse are protected; ascendants are also protected today. The government proposed in 2023 (BuA 123/2023) to abolish the Pflichtteil of ascendants. Exact fractions not confirmed.
succession.foreign_law_note: Not under the EU Regulation. The Private International Law Act (IPRG) art. 29 generally ties succession to the deceased's nationality, so a foreign national normally keeps home-country law. Art. 29 para. 5 adds a double filter on claims against foundations or trusts that received assets in life.
succession.trust_note: The Hague Trusts Convention is in force since 1 April 2006 (HCCH table: accession). Liechtenstein has its own trust law (Persons and Companies Act, PGR, Treuhänderschaft) and foundation law (PGR art. 552 ff.), and family foundations are allowed. Art. 29(5) IPRG limits the use of foundations or trusts to defeat forced heirs.
open_questions: Status of the 2023 inheritance reform (BuA 123/2023) after first reading in December 2023 was not found.
Pflichtteil fractions, PGR article numbers and the text of IPRG art. 29 para. 1 were not verified.
Whether foreigners may make a formal choice of law (Rechtswahl) beyond the nationality default was not confirmed.

immigration.name: Liechtenstein
immigration.summary: Liechtenstein is in the EEA but keeps a quota on residence permits. EU/EEA citizens who work get permits from an annual quota (at least 56, half by lottery), and a separate small quota of 16 a year covers EEA citizens who live on their own capital. US and other citizens can only get a permit if they have a job or real economic significance for the country; residence cannot be bought. A lump-sum tax (25% of living costs) exists for new residents who do not work.
immigration.naturalisation: Not researched this session. Earlier practice: long residence (reported about 10 years) plus a municipal vote; not verified.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Not verified this session; Liechtenstein has generally required renunciation of other nationalities, with exceptions. See open questions.

routes.name: EEA nationals: residence permit within the annual quota (employed)
routes.summary: EEA citizens with a job in Liechtenstein get residence from a yearly quota; the EEA agreement allows Liechtenstein to cap numbers, so there is no free right to move.
routes.requirements: Quota of at least 56 new residence permits a year for EEA nationals working in Liechtenstein, plus around 300 short-term permits (up to 12 months); half the long-term permits are allocated by the government on application and half by lottery (28 a year in the employed lottery). Swiss and UK nationals are not eligible for the EEA lottery; Swiss have their own channel of about 17 places.
routes.physical_presence: Residence in Liechtenstein for the permit

routes.name: EEA nationals: quota permit without gainful activity
routes.summary: A small separate quota of 16 permits a year is open to EEA citizens who do not work and live on their own funds.
routes.requirements: Supplementary quota of 16 new permits a year for EEA nationals not exercising an economic activity (another source says about 20); sufficient own means. No numeric financial threshold published in the sources found. Applications compete for few places.

routes.name: Non-EEA nationals: permit for employment or economic significance
routes.summary: US and other citizens are admitted only in small numbers: with a job offer from a Liechtenstein employer or because they are of real economic significance to the country.
routes.requirements: Employment contract or real economic significance; limited annual permits. 'There is no direct purchase of residence through an investment' (private.law wiki). Exact quota numbers (one source claims about 89 a year) not confirmed.

routes.name: Lump-sum taxation for new residents
routes.summary: New residents who do not work in Liechtenstein can agree a tax of 25% of their worldwide living costs. It still needs a residence permit first.
routes.requirements: Tax Act arts. 30-33 as summarised by private.law wiki: not a Liechtenstein citizen, new to the country or back after at least 10 years away, no local gainful activity, living on foreign income or wealth. Amount agreed with the Fiscal Authority; no fixed minimum in the current Act.
routes.tax_note: Replaces ordinary income and wealth tax on a living-cost base; not an immigration permit.

open_questions: Official llv.li (Migration and Passport Office) pages returned 403; quota numbers come from an EU Commission review and secondary sources.
Government fees for permits not sourced.
Financial thresholds for the non-gainful EEA quota not published in sources found.
Years until permanent residence, naturalisation period and dual-citizenship rules not verified.
Lottery dates and exact split between lottery and government allocation are unconfirmed.
Lump-sum tax summary comes from a secondary wiki; statute not checked.
